subject: geography

moments.title: Agassiz on Ice Ages
moments.body: Agassiz presents his Ice Age theory to the Swiss Society of Natural Sciences. He argues that erratic boulders, polished rocks and moraines across northern Europe and the Alps record a former massive glaciation, not the biblical Flood.
moments.takeaway: Most contemporaries rejected the theory. Agassiz's 1840 'Études sur les glaciers' set out the case in detail; acceptance came over decades.

moments.title: Milankovitch cycles
moments.body: Milankovic calculates how Earth's orbital eccentricity, axial tilt and precession vary on roughly 100,000-, 41,000- and 23,000-year cycles, and how these affect solar input. He proposes these as the pacemaker of glacial cycles. Published in detail in 1941.
moments.takeaway: Milankovic's work was largely ignored until ocean cores in the 1970s (Hays, Imbrie and Shackleton, 1976) directly confirmed his frequencies in marine sediment δ¹⁸O records.

moments.title: Ice cores deliver the record
moments.body: Camp Century (1966), Vostok (1985, 1998 extended), EPICA Dome C (2004) ice cores reveal a continuous record of CO2, methane and temperature proxies across 800,000 years. The Milankovitch frequencies appear strongly.
moments.takeaway: Glacial cycles are orbitally paced but amplified by feedbacks (ice-albedo, CO2). The ice age framework is now mainstream physics, not contested speculation.

now.title: Anthropocene against the cycles
now.body: Atmospheric CO2 is now above 420 ppm — outside the entire 800,000-year Vostok-EPICA range (typically 180-300 ppm). The expected next glaciation in orbital terms would be in around 50,000 years, but current CO2 is likely to delay or skip it.
now.open_questions: How sensitively does the climate system respond to forcing? Climate sensitivity — the warming for a doubling of CO2 — is the central uncertainty (IPCC AR6: likely range 2.5-4 °C).

reflection: Quaternary science is one of geology's great syntheses — orbital astronomy, geomorphology, isotope chemistry, ocean drilling. The result is a planetary climate history of extraordinary detail, and a baseline against which to read the present.
